# Indicators

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_indicator_docs.py from oda_data._registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

oda-data has 46 indicators. Each id names who defines it (`oecd` or `one`), the table it reads, and what it counts. `oda.indicators()` returns this list as a DataFrame and `oda.describe(id)` prints one entry.

An indicator's kind says how it is computed. A `sum` adds a value over the table's rows. A `ratio` divides the sum of its numerators by the sum of its denominators, in current USD, so it takes no `unit=`. A `derived` indicator adds or subtracts other indicators, each on the basis of each year. A `method` runs ONE's own code, such as the imputation of multilateral sectors, and then takes units, groups, and `by=` like any other indicator.

A basis marked "2018 on" or "2010 on" raises `BasisRangeError` for earlier years. A caveat that names a basis or years in brackets warns with `OdaDataWarning` when a call reads that basis in those years.

## DAC1

DAC1 holds each provider's official totals, one published line per kind of flow. Its indicators answer how much a provider gave.

### `oecd.dac1.total_oda`

Official development assistance from each provider. Read from line 1010 on cash bases and line 11010 on grant equivalents.

- Name: Total ODA
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `year`, `flow`
- Bases: `headline` (default), `net_disbursement`, `gross_disbursement`, `commitment`, `grant_equivalent` (2018 on)
- Default providers: DAC countries (`oda.groups.dac_countries`)
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.dac1.total_oda", years=2023)
```

### `oecd.dac1.lines`

Any published DAC1 line that is an amount of money, named with lines=. Lines nest, so each line is its own row and no two lines are summed. Net flows by default. A line the basis's flow does not publish, such as GNI (line 1) on grant equivalents, raises and names the bases that hold it.

- Name: DAC1 lines
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `year`, `line`, `flow`
- Bases: `net_disbursement` (default), `headline`, `gross_disbursement`, `commitment`, `grant_equivalent` (2015 on)
- Default providers: DAC countries (`oda.groups.dac_countries`)
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise
- Caveat: Grant equivalents cover only the 25 to 27 DAC members that reported them before they became the headline basis in 2018 (grant_equivalent basis, 2015 to 2017).

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.dac1.lines", years=2023, by=["provider", "line"])
```

Total ODA less in-donor refugee costs (line 1820), in-donor student costs (line 1500) and debt relief (line 1600). Administrative costs stay in. Each line is read on the basis of each year, so the headline basis subtracts grant equivalents from 2018.

- Kind: derived
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `year`, `flow`

### `one.dac1.total_oda_eu_attributed`

Total ODA, with the row of EU Institutions (918) reduced by what every other provider paid them that year (line 2102 on the same basis), so 918 adds up with any of its funders without counting that money twice. Every other provider's row is its total ODA. 918's row is the same whichever providers the call names; oecd.dac1.total_oda gives 918's own spending.

- Name: Total ODA, EU Institutions net of their funders
- Kind: method
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `year`
- Bases: `headline` (default), `net_disbursement`, `gross_disbursement`, `commitment`, `grant_equivalent` (2018 on)
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise
- Caveat: 918's row is negative in a year in which its funders' recorded contributions exceed the ODA EU Institutions report.
- Caveat: 918's row in DAC1's last year is null until the providers that paid it the year before report line 2102; allow_partial=True nets the contributions reported so far.

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("one.dac1.total_oda_eu_attributed", years=2023)
```

### `one.dac1.gni`

The provider's GNI (line 1, net flows), and for EU Institutions (918) the summed GNI of the countries that were EU members in each year, the United Kingdom to 2020 included. A member with no GNI in a year between two it reported counts as zero, and explain() names it. In a year after a member's last GNI, 918 has a null GNI unless allow_partial=True. one.dac1.gni_fixed_eu27 gives 918 today's EU27 in every year.

- Name: Gross national income, EU Institutions included
- Kind: method
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `year`
- Bases: `net_disbursement` (default)
- Default providers: DAC countries (`oda.groups.dac_countries`)
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("one.dac1.gni", years=2023)
```

### `one.dac1.gni_fixed_eu27`

The provider's GNI (line 1, net flows), and for EU Institutions (918) the summed GNI of today's 27 EU members in every year, so the United Kingdom is excluded. A member with no GNI in a year between two it reported counts as zero, and explain() names it. In a year after a member's last GNI, 918 has a null GNI unless allow_partial=True. one.dac1.gni gives 918 the members of each year.

- Name: Gross national income, EU Institutions as today's EU27
- Kind: method
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `year`
- Bases: `net_disbursement` (default)
- Default providers: DAC countries (`oda.groups.dac_countries`)
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("one.dac1.gni_fixed_eu27", years=2023)
```

Name 918 to see it. one.dac1.oda_gni_ratio_fixed_eu27 uses today's EU27 in every year.

Total ODA as a percentage of GNI, as oecd.dac1.oda_gni_ratio, plus a ratio for EU Institutions (918) over the GNI of today's 27 EU members in every year (one.dac1.gni_fixed_eu27). Name 918 to see it. one.dac1.oda_gni_ratio uses the members of each year, the United Kingdom to 2020 included.

## DAC2A

DAC2A holds what each recipient receives from each provider, net of repayments. Its indicators answer who received the money.

### `oecd.dac2a.recipient_oda`

ODA each recipient receives from each provider: net disbursements (line 206) by default, and gross disbursements (line 240) on request.

- Name: ODA received
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `year`
- Bases: `headline` (default), `net_disbursement`, `gross_disbursement`
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise
- Caveat: Summed over providers, recipient totals fall short of the OECD's official donors total (provider 20005), which also holds non-DAC estimates that no provider reports by recipient. On line 206 the gap is Saudi Arabia's ODA that appears in its developing-countries total (10100) only, from USD 0.6bn to USD 6.4bn a year from 2015 (USD 4.5bn in 2024). Pass providers=20005 for that total.

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.dac2a.recipient_oda", years=2023, by=["provider", "recipient"])
```

### `oecd.dac2a.imputed_multilateral_oda`

The share of multilateral organisations' outflows to each recipient that the OECD attributes to each provider's core contributions (line 106). Multilateral providers are left out, since the shares are their own flows.

- Name: Imputed multilateral ODA
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `year`
- Bases: `headline` (default), `net_disbursement`
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise
- Caveat: Summed over providers, recipient totals fall short of the OECD's official donors total (provider 20005), which also holds non-DAC estimates that no provider reports by recipient. On line 106 the gap is Saudi Arabia's imputed shares that appear in its developing-countries total (10100) only, from USD 16m to USD 417m a year from 2017 (USD 417m in 2024).

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.dac2a.imputed_multilateral_oda", years=2023, by=["provider", "recipient"])
```

### `oecd.dac2a.technical_cooperation`

Grants that pay for know-how, training, research, and the experts who provide them, by recipient (line 207).

- Name: Technical co-operation
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `year`
- Bases: `headline` (default), `net_disbursement`
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise
- Caveat: Summed over providers, recipient totals fall short of the OECD's official donors total (provider 20005), which also holds non-DAC estimates that no provider reports by recipient. On line 207 the gap is Saudi Arabia's technical co-operation that appears in its developing-countries total (10100) only, from USD 21m to USD 159m a year in 2015-2021 and none from 2022. Pass providers=20005 for that total.

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.dac2a.technical_cooperation", years=2023, by=["provider", "recipient"])
```

### `oecd.dac2a.lines`

Any published DAC2A line that is an amount of money, named with lines=. Each line carries its own basis. Net disbursements are the default (line 206 and its parts), and lines 204 and 240 read gross disbursements with basis='gross_disbursement'. Lines nest, so each line is its own row and no two lines are summed. A line counts the rows its named indicator counts, so line 106 leaves out multilateral providers as oecd.dac2a.imputed_multilateral_oda does.

- Name: DAC2A lines
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `year`, `line`
- Bases: `net_disbursement` (default), `gross_disbursement`
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.dac2a.lines", years=2023, by=["provider", "recipient"])
```

### `one.dac2a.recipient_oda_with_imputed_multilateral`

Each provider's net ODA to each recipient (line 206) plus its imputed share of multilateral organisations' outflows to that recipient (line 106). Multilateral providers are left out, since the imputed shares are their own flows. Net disbursements only, the one basis of line 106.

- Name: ODA received, imputed multilateral included
- Kind: derived
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `year`
- Bases: `headline` (default), `net_disbursement`
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("one.dac2a.recipient_oda_with_imputed_multilateral", years=2023, by=["provider", "recipient"])
```

## CRS

The Creditor Reporting System holds one row per activity, with its sector, channel, modality, finance type, and policy markers.

### `oecd.crs.bilateral_oda`

Bilateral ODA reported activity by activity. It is category 10 (categories 10 and 60 on grant equivalents) with bi_multi 1, 3, 7 or 8.

- Name: Bilateral ODA
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `sector`, `broad_sector`, `channel`, `modality`, `flow`, `finance_type`, `year`
- Bases: `gross_disbursement` (default), `commitment`, `net_disbursement`, `grant_equivalent` (2018 on)
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise
- Caveat: CRS totals differ from DAC1 totals. Use oecd.dac1.bilateral_oda for headline figures.

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.crs.bilateral_oda", years=2023, by=["provider", "broad_sector"])
```

### `oecd.crs.multilateral_oda`

ODA multilateral organisations give from their own resources, reported activity by activity. It is category 10 with bi_multi 4, on cash bases only, since the CRS gives these flows no grant equivalent. The providers are the organisations, except EU Institutions (918), which report as bilateral (bi_multi 1), so their outflows (USD 40.0bn in 2023) sit in oecd.crs.bilateral_oda. Members' core contributions to the organisations are oecd.dac1.multilateral_oda.

- Name: Multilateral ODA
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `sector`, `broad_sector`, `channel`, `modality`, `flow`, `finance_type`, `year`
- Bases: `gross_disbursement` (default), `commitment`, `net_disbursement`
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.crs.multilateral_oda", years=2023, by=["provider", "broad_sector"])
```

### `oecd.crs.bilateral_oof`

Official flows that are not ODA, such as loans on market terms, reported activity by activity. They are category 21 with bi_multi 1, 3, 7 or 8 and have no grant equivalent.

- Name: Bilateral other official flows
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `sector`, `broad_sector`, `channel`, `modality`, `flow`, `finance_type`, `year`
- Bases: `gross_disbursement` (default), `commitment`, `net_disbursement`
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.crs.bilateral_oof", years=2023, by=["provider", "broad_sector"])
```

### `oecd.crs.multilateral_oof`

Other official flows multilateral organisations give from their own resources, such as loans on market terms, reported activity by activity. They are category 21 with bi_multi 4 and have no grant equivalent. The providers are the organisations.

- Name: Multilateral other official flows
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `sector`, `broad_sector`, `channel`, `modality`, `flow`, `finance_type`, `year`
- Bases: `gross_disbursement` (default), `commitment`, `net_disbursement`
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.crs.multilateral_oof", years=2023, by=["provider", "broad_sector"])
```

### `oecd.crs.private_development_finance`

Development finance from private foundations, reported activity by activity. It is CRS category 30, mostly bi_multi 6, and has no grant equivalent. The foundations' core contributions to multilateral organisations (bi_multi 2) are left out, since the organisations' own outflows count that money again. By default the providers are the private foundations in oda.groups.private_donors; a few official providers report category 30 rows of their own country's private flows, which a call that names them reads.

- Name: Private development finance
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `sector`, `broad_sector`, `channel`, `modality`, `flow`, `finance_type`, `year`
- Bases: `gross_disbursement` (default), `commitment`, `net_disbursement`
- Default providers: Private donors (`oda.groups.private_donors`)
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.crs.private_development_finance", years=2023, by=["provider", "broad_sector"])
```

### `oecd.crs.gender_marker`

Bilateral allocable ODA by its gender equality policy marker score: principal, significant, not_targeted or not_screened. Group by score to split it. Summed over scores it is all bilateral allocable ODA. It starts in 2010, the first year the CRS records the aid type of nearly every activity.

- Name: Bilateral allocable ODA by gender equality marker
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `sector`, `broad_sector`, `channel`, `modality`, `flow`, `finance_type`, `year`, `score`
- Bases: `gross_disbursement` (default, 2010 on), `commitment` (2010 on), `net_disbursement` (2010 on), `grant_equivalent` (2018 on)
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.crs.gender_marker", years=2023, by=["provider", "broad_sector"])
```

Bilateral allocable ODA by its environment policy marker score: principal, significant, not_targeted or not_screened. Group by score to split it. Summed over scores it is all bilateral allocable ODA. It starts in 2010, the first year the CRS records the aid type of nearly every activity.

- Name: Bilateral allocable ODA by environment marker
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `sector`, `broad_sector`, `channel`, `modality`, `flow`, `finance_type`, `year`, `score`
- Bases: `gross_disbursement` (default, 2010 on), `commitment` (2010 on), `net_disbursement` (2010 on), `grant_equivalent` (2018 on)
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.crs.environment_marker", years=2023, by=["provider", "broad_sector"])
```

### `oecd.crs.dig_marker`

Bilateral allocable ODA by its participatory development and good governance policy marker score: principal, significant, not_targeted or not_screened. Group by score to split it. Summed over scores it is all bilateral allocable ODA. It starts in 2010, the first year the CRS records the aid type of nearly every activity.

- Name: Bilateral allocable ODA by participatory development and good governance marker
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `sector`, `broad_sector`, `channel`, `modality`, `flow`, `finance_type`, `year`, `score`
- Bases: `gross_disbursement` (default, 2010 on), `commitment` (2010 on), `net_disbursement` (2010 on), `grant_equivalent` (2018 on)
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.crs.dig_marker", years=2023, by=["provider", "broad_sector"])
```

### `one.crs.covid_oda`

Bilateral ODA whose CRS keywords include #COVID-19, the tag the OECD asks providers to give activities that respond to the pandemic. Its rows are otherwise those of oecd.crs.bilateral_oda.

- Name: COVID-19 ODA
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `sector`, `broad_sector`, `channel`, `modality`, `flow`, `finance_type`, `year`
- Bases: `gross_disbursement` (default), `commitment`, `net_disbursement`, `grant_equivalent` (2018 on)
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise
- Caveat: CRS totals differ from DAC1 totals. Use oecd.dac1.bilateral_oda for headline figures.
- Caveat: Providers tag activities with #COVID-19 from 2020, and some leave the tag off activities that respond to the pandemic.

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("one.crs.covid_oda", years=2023, by=["provider", "broad_sector"])
```

## Multisystem

The Multisystem table holds providers' contributions to each multilateral organisation and fund.

### `oecd.multisystem.core_contributions`

Providers' core (unearmarked) contributions to multilateral organisations and funds, by channel. These are the Multisystem rows 'Core contributions to' in current prices; earmarked money sent through a channel is bilateral and sits in oecd.crs.bilateral_oda.

- Name: Core contributions to multilateral organisations
- Kind: sum
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `channel`, `year`
- Bases: `gross_disbursement` (default), `commitment`
- Default providers: DAC countries (`oda.groups.dac_countries`)
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("oecd.multisystem.core_contributions", years=2023, by=["provider", "channel"])
```

### `one.crs.imputed_multilateral_oda`

Each provider's core contributions to multilateral organisations, spread across recipients and sectors in the proportions each organisation spends its own money in the CRS over three years. allocation_status says how each amount was spread: imputed, stale_share, proxy or unallocated.

- Name: Imputed multilateral ODA
- Kind: method
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `recipient`, `sector`, `broad_sector`, `channel`, `allocation_status`, `year`
- Bases: `gross_disbursement` (default), `commitment`
- Default providers: every official provider in the table, aggregates excluded; EU Institutions (918) are left out of a sum across providers and shown when split by provider
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise
- Caveat: Shares come from each organisation's CRS gross disbursements of ODA and other official flows. Unallocated amounts and fixed-purpose proxies have no recipient, so a filter on recipients leaves them out.

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("one.crs.imputed_multilateral_oda", years=2023, by=["provider", "broad_sector"])
```

### `one.crs.bilateral_plus_multilateral_oda`

Bilateral ODA from the CRS (oecd.crs.bilateral_oda) plus core contributions to multilateral organisations from the Multisystem table (oecd.multisystem.core_contributions), on gross disbursements or commitments, the bases both tables share.

- Name: Bilateral and multilateral ODA, activity data
- Kind: derived
- Version: 1
- Dimensions: `provider`, `year`
- Bases: `gross_disbursement` (default), `commitment`
- Default providers: DAC countries (`oda.groups.dac_countries`)
- Values: USD millions unless `unit=` says otherwise

```python
import oda_data as oda

oda.get("one.crs.bilateral_plus_multilateral_oda", years=2023)
```
